96: /// Load and validate a `SeaSourceSet` through `domainforge-core`.
97: ///
98: /// Returns a `DomainModel` on success, or `domain_model_error` on any parse,
99: /// validation, or source-hash failure. No side effects.
100: pub fn load_validate(source_set: &SeaSourceSet) -> Result<DomainModel, ForgeError> {
101:     // Find the entry source.
102:     let entry = source_set
103:         .files
104:         .iter()
105:         .find(|f| f.uri == source_set.entry_uri)
106:         .ok_or_else(|| ForgeError::Input("entry source not found in source set".into()))?;
107: 
108:     // Verify source hash matches declared hash.
109:     let computed_hash = sha256_content(&entry.content);
110:     if computed_hash != entry.sha256 {
111:         return Err(ForgeError::Internal(format!(
112:             "domain_model_error: source hash drift for {entry_uri}: declared={declared} computed={computed_hash}",
113:             entry_uri = entry.uri,
114:             declared = entry.sha256,
115:         )));
116:     }
117: 
118:     // Parse through domainforge-core.
119:     let options = ParseOptions::default();
120:     let graph = parse_to_graph_with_options(&entry.content, &options)
121:         .map_err(|e| ForgeError::Internal(format!("domain_model_error: parse failed: {e}")))?;
122: 
123:     // Validate the graph.
124:     let validation = graph.validate();
125:     if validation.error_count > 0 {
126:         let errors: Vec<String> = validation
127:             .violations
128:             .iter()
129:             .filter(|v| v.severity == Severity::Error)
130:             .map(|v| format!("{}: {}", v.policy_name, v.message))
131:             .collect();
132:         return Err(ForgeError::Internal(format!(
133:             "domain_model_error: semantic validation failed: {}",
134:             errors.join("; ")
135:         )));
136:     }
137: 
138:     // Build source_refs (sorted).
139:     let mut source_refs: Vec<SourceRef> = source_set
140:         .files
141:         .iter()
142:         .map(|f| SourceRef {
143:             uri: f.uri.clone(),
144:             sha256: f.sha256.clone(),
145:         })
146:         .collect();
147:     source_refs.sort();
148: 
149:     // Build parse_options_sha256.
150:     let parse_options_value = serde_json::json!({
151:         "namespace_registry": null,
152:         "entry_path": source_set.entry_uri,
153:     });
154:     let parse_options_sha256 = sha256_json(&parse_options_value)?;
155: 
156:     // Build semantic_model_sha256 over the canonical 4-tuple.
157:     let canonical_tuple = serde_json::json!({
158:         "domainforge_version": domainforge_core::VERSION,
159:         "adapter_descriptor_sha256": ADAPTER_DESCRIPTOR_SHA256,
160:         "parse_options_sha256": parse_options_sha256,
161:         "source_refs": source_refs,
162:     });
163:     let semantic_model_sha256 = sha256_json(&canonical_tuple)?;
164: 
165:     // Extract concept refs from the graph (sorted).
166:     let mut concept_refs: Vec<String> = graph
167:         .all_entities()
168:         .iter()
169:         .map(|e| e.name().to_string())
170:         .collect();
171:     concept_refs.extend(graph.all_resources().iter().map(|r| r.name().to_string()));
172:     concept_refs.sort();
173:     concept_refs.dedup();
174:     let mut class_refs: Vec<String> = graph
175:         .all_resources()
176:         .iter()
177:         .map(|resource| resource.name().to_string())
178:         .collect();
179:     class_refs.sort();
180:     class_refs.dedup();
181: 
182:     let model_ref = DomainModelRef {
183:         source_refs,
184:         domainforge_version: domainforge_core::VERSION.to_string(),
185:         adapter_descriptor_sha256: ADAPTER_DESCRIPTOR_SHA256.into(),
186:         parse_options_sha256,
187:         semantic_model_sha256,
188:         concept_refs,
189:         class_refs,
190:         validation_evidence_refs: vec![format!(
191:             "validation:error_count={}",
192:             validation.error_count
193:         )],
194:     };
195: 
196:     Ok(DomainModel { graph, model_ref })
197: }

199: /// Normalize a DomainForge authority decision to a SEA Forge candidate disposition.
200: ///
201: /// | DomainForge result | SEA Forge candidate disposition |
202: /// |---|---|
203: /// | `Reject` or `Deny` | `deny` |
204: /// | `Escalate` | `escalate` |
205: /// | `Allow` | `allow` |
206: /// | `NotApplicable` | no candidate; `deny` if policy requires DomainForge |
207: pub fn normalize_authority(raw_decision: &str) -> CandidateDisposition {
208:     match raw_decision {
209:         "Allow" => CandidateDisposition::Allow,
210:         "Reject" | "Deny" => CandidateDisposition::Deny,
211:         "Escalate" => CandidateDisposition::Escalate,
212:         _ => CandidateDisposition::Deny, // NotApplicable or unknown → deny-if-required
213:     }
214: }

216: pub fn evaluate_authority(
217:     model: &DomainModel,
218:     operation_kind: &str,
219:     resource_id: &str,
220:     evidence_refs: Vec<String>,
221: ) -> Result<DomainForgeTrace, ForgeError> {
222:     if evidence_refs.is_empty() || model.model_ref.validation_evidence_refs.is_empty() {
223:         return Err(ForgeError::Input(
224:             "DomainForge authority evaluation requires validation evidence".into(),
225:         ));
226:     }
227:     let semantic_target = std::path::Path::new(resource_id)
228:         .file_stem()
229:         .and_then(|stem| stem.to_str())
230:         .is_some_and(|target| {
231:             model
232:                 .graph
233:                 .all_entities()
234:                 .iter()
235:                 .any(|entity| entity.name().eq_ignore_ascii_case(target))
236:                 || model
237:                     .graph
238:                     .all_resources()
239:                     .iter()
240:                     .any(|resource| resource.name().eq_ignore_ascii_case(target))
241:         });
242:     let raw_decision = match (operation_kind, semantic_target) {
243:         ("write_file", true) => "Allow",
244:         ("write_file", false) => "Reject",
245:         ("execute_command", _) => "NotApplicable",
246:         _ => "NotApplicable",
247:     };
248:     Ok(DomainForgeTrace {
249:         raw_decision: raw_decision.into(),
250:         normalized_disposition: normalize_authority(raw_decision),
251:         reason: "DomainForge evaluated validated model against canonical action".into(),
252:         evidence_refs,
253:     })
254: }

256: /// In-memory projection of a DomainModel into CALM or RDF.
257: ///
258: /// Pure: no filesystem writes, no network calls, no CLI invocations.
259: /// Returns a sorted map of relative_path → content (§7.0a, §10.4a).
260: pub fn project(
261:     model: &DomainModel,
262:     kind: &ProjectionKind,
263: ) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, ForgeError> {
264:     match kind {
265:         ProjectionKind::Calm => {
266:             let mut calm_value = domainforge_core::calm::export(&model.graph).map_err(|e| {
267:                 ForgeError::Internal(format!("domain_model_error: CALM projection failed: {e}"))
268:             })?;
269:             // Strip non-deterministic timestamp for byte-identical regeneration (§10.7).
270:             // domainforge-core adds sea:timestamp to metadata; remove it so the same
271:             // graph produces identical bytes across calls.
272:             if let Some(metadata) = calm_value
273:                 .get_mut("metadata")
274:                 .and_then(|m| m.as_object_mut())
275:             {
276:                 metadata.remove("sea:timestamp");
277:             }
278:             let mut map = BTreeMap::new();
279:             let encoded = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&calm_value)
280:                 .map_err(|e| ForgeError::Serialization(e.to_string()))?;
281:             map.insert(
282:                 "calm.json".into(),
283:                 String::from_utf8_lossy(&encoded).into_owned(),
284:             );
285:             Ok(map)
286:         }
287:         ProjectionKind::Rdf => {
288:             let kg =
289:                 domainforge_core::kg::KnowledgeGraph::from_graph(&model.graph).map_err(|e| {
290:                     ForgeError::Internal(format!("domain_model_error: KG build failed: {e}"))
291:                 })?;
292:             let turtle = kg.to_turtle();
293:             let rdf_xml = kg.to_rdf_xml();
294:             let mut map = BTreeMap::new();
295:             map.insert("model.ttl".into(), turtle);
296:             map.insert("model.rdf".into(), rdf_xml);
297:             Ok(map)
298:         }
299:         ProjectionKind::Kg => {
300:             // M9 (E11): the self-model knowledge-graph projection. The KG is the
301:             // canonical Turtle serialization of the validated graph.
302:             let kg =
303:                 domainforge_core::kg::KnowledgeGraph::from_graph(&model.graph).map_err(|e| {
304:                     ForgeError::Internal(format!("domain_model_error: KG build failed: {e}"))
305:                 })?;
306:             let turtle = kg.to_turtle();
307:             let mut map = BTreeMap::new();
308:             map.insert("model.ttl".into(), turtle);
309:             Ok(map)
310:         }
311:         _ => Err(ForgeError::Input(format!(
312:             "unsupported projection kind for DomainForge adapter: {kind:?}"
313:         ))),
314:     }
315: }

80: /// Move-only proof that one exact action may execute in one exact context.
81: /// It is intentionally not serializable or cloneable.
82: pub struct ActionGrant {
83:     action: AuthorityAction,
84:     run_id: String,
85:     plan_item_id: String,
86:     workspace_root: PathBuf,
87:     artifacts_root: Option<PathBuf>,
88:     timeout_secs: Option<u64>,
89:     env_keys: BTreeSet<String>,
90:     _assurance_ref: Option<String>,
91:     sandbox_class: String,
92:     boundaries: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
93:     compensating_controls: Vec<String>,
94:     expires_at: chrono::DateTime<Utc>,
95: }
96: 
97: impl ActionGrant {
98:     pub fn sandbox_class(&self) -> &str {
99:         &self.sandbox_class
100:     }
101: 
102:     /// Authority-derived TCP ports this grant permits a jail-class run to bind
103:     /// and connect to, projected from the `network` boundary dimension.
104:     ///
105:     /// Absent or empty means "no network" (fail-closed default): a jail run may
106:     /// not open outbound TCP connections or bind/listen on TCP sockets. Values
107:     /// that do not parse as a `u16` TCP port are ignored, so a malformed policy
108:     /// value can only ever *narrow* the granted scope, never widen it. This is
109:     /// derived from policy/authority, never from child-controlled input.
110:     pub fn network_tcp_ports(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
111:         let mut ports: Vec<u16> = self
112:             .boundaries
113:             .get("network")
114:             .into_iter()
115:             .flatten()
116:             .filter_map(|value| value.parse::<u16>().ok())
117:             .collect();
118:         ports.sort_unstable();
119:         ports.dedup();
120:         ports
121:     }
122: 
123:     pub fn authorize(
124:         self,
125:         action: &AuthorityAction,
126:         run_id: &str,
127:         plan_item_id: &str,
128:         workspace_root: &Path,
129:     ) -> Result<(), ForgeError> {
130:         self.authorize_with_controls(action, run_id, plan_item_id, workspace_root, &[])
131:     }
132: 
133:     pub fn authorize_with_controls(
134:         self,
135:         action: &AuthorityAction,
136:         run_id: &str,
137:         plan_item_id: &str,
138:         workspace_root: &Path,
139:         compensating_controls: &[String],
140:     ) -> Result<(), ForgeError> {
141:         if Utc::now() > self.expires_at {
142:             return Err(ForgeError::Input("authority grant expired".into()));
143:         }
144:         if &self.action != action
145:             || self.run_id != run_id
146:             || self.plan_item_id != plan_item_id
147:             || self.workspace_root != workspace_root
148:         {
149:             return Err(ForgeError::Input(
150:                 "authority grant does not match action context".into(),
151:             ));
152:         }
153:         if self.compensating_controls != compensating_controls {
154:             return Err(ForgeError::Input(
155:                 "authority grant compensating controls mismatch".into(),
156:             ));
157:         }
158:         if let Some(allowed) = self.boundaries.get("workspace") {
159:             let workspace = workspace_root.to_string_lossy();
160:             if !allowed.iter().any(|value| value == workspace.as_ref()) {
161:                 return Err(ForgeError::Input(
162:                     "authority grant workspace is outside its boundary".into(),
163:                 ));
164:             }
165:         }
166:         if let Some(allowed) = self.boundaries.get("sandbox_class") {
167:             if !allowed.contains(&self.sandbox_class) {
168:                 return Err(ForgeError::Input(
169:                     "authority grant sandbox is outside its boundary".into(),
170:                 ));
171:             }
172:         }
173:         Ok(())
174:     }
175: 
176:     pub fn authorize_execution(
177:         self,
178:         action: &AuthorityAction,
179:         context: ExecutionGrantContext<'_>,
180:     ) -> Result<(), ForgeError> {
181:         if self.artifacts_root.as_deref() != Some(context.artifacts_root)
182:             || self.timeout_secs != Some(context.timeout_secs)
183:             || self.env_keys != context.env_keys
184:         {
185:             return Err(ForgeError::Input(
186:                 "authority grant does not match execution context".into(),
187:             ));
188:         }
189:         if let Some(allowed) = self.boundaries.get("artifacts_root") {
190:             let artifacts = context.artifacts_root.to_string_lossy();
191:             if !allowed.iter().any(|value| value == artifacts.as_ref()) {
192:                 return Err(ForgeError::Input(
193:                     "authority grant artifacts root is outside its boundary".into(),
194:                 ));
195:             }
196:         }
197:         if let Some(allowed) = self.boundaries.get("timeout_secs") {
198:             if !allowed
199:                 .iter()
200:                 .any(|value| value == &context.timeout_secs.to_string())
201:             {
202:                 return Err(ForgeError::Input(
203:                     "authority grant timeout is outside its boundary".into(),
204:                 ));
205:             }
206:         }
207:         if let Some(allowed) = self.boundaries.get("env_keys") {
208:             if context.env_keys.iter().any(|key| !allowed.contains(key)) {
209:                 return Err(ForgeError::Input(
210:                     "authority grant environment is outside its boundary".into(),
211:                 ));
212:             }
213:         }
214:         if self.compensating_controls.contains(&"short_timeout".into()) && context.timeout_secs > 30
215:         {
216:             return Err(ForgeError::Input(
217:                 "short_timeout compensating control not satisfied".into(),
218:             ));
219:         }
220:         if self
221:             .compensating_controls
222:             .contains(&"minimal_environment".into())
223:             && context
224:                 .env_keys
225:                 .iter()
226:                 .any(|key| !matches!(key.as_str(), "PATH" | "HOME"))
227:         {
228:             return Err(ForgeError::Input(
229:                 "minimal_environment compensating control not satisfied".into(),
230:             ));
231:         }
232:         self.authorize_with_controls(
233:             action,
234:             context.run_id,
235:             context.plan_item_id,
236:             context.workspace_root,
237:             context.compensating_controls,
238:         )
239:     }
240: }

258: impl DomainForgeCandidate {
259:     pub fn evaluate(
260:         model: &DomainModel,
261:         action: &AuthorityAction,
262:         evidence_refs: Vec<String>,
263:     ) -> Result<Self, ForgeError> {
264:         let (operation_kind, resource_id) = match action {
265:             AuthorityAction::WriteFile { path, .. } => ("write_file", path.as_str()),
266:             AuthorityAction::ExecuteCommand { argv, .. } => (
267:                 "execute_command",
268:                 argv.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
269:             ),
270:             AuthorityAction::Reserved {
271:                 resource_type,
272:                 resource_id,
273:                 ..
274:             } => (resource_type.as_str(), resource_id.as_str()),
275:             AuthorityAction::ExternalApi { host } => ("external_api", host.as_str()),
276:             AuthorityAction::AgentProbe { host, .. } => ("external_api", host.as_str()),
277:             AuthorityAction::AgentTask { host, .. } => ("external_api", host.as_str()),
278:             AuthorityAction::GitCommit { .. } => ("git_commit", "repository"),
279:             AuthorityAction::GithubPr { .. } => ("github_pr", "pull_request"),
280:             AuthorityAction::Unclassified { .. } => ("unclassified", "unknown"),
281:         };
282:         let trace = evaluate_authority(model, operation_kind, resource_id, evidence_refs)?;
283:         Ok(Self {
284:             disposition: trace.normalized_disposition.clone(),
285:             trace,
286:             model_ref: model.model_ref.clone(),
287:         })
288:     }
289: }

291: pub fn resolve_candidates(
292:     candidates: &[GovernanceVerdict],
293:     policy: &ResolutionPolicy,
294: ) -> ResolvedGovernance {
295:     let mut boundaries = BTreeMap::<String, BTreeSet<String>>::new();
296:     let mut empty_boundary = false;
297:     for candidate in candidates {
298:         for (dimension, allowed) in &candidate.boundaries {
299:             boundaries
300:                 .entry(dimension.clone())
301:                 .and_modify(|current| {
302:                     current.retain(|value| allowed.contains(value));
303:                     empty_boundary |= current.is_empty();
304:                 })
305:                 .or_insert_with(|| allowed.clone());
306:         }
307:     }
308:     let compensating_controls: BTreeSet<String> = candidates
309:         .iter()
310:         .flat_map(|candidate| candidate.compensating_controls.iter().cloned())
311:         .collect();
312:     let missing_evidence = candidates
313:         .iter()
314:         .any(|candidate| candidate.evidence_refs.is_empty());
315:     let has = |disposition| {
316:         candidates
317:             .iter()
318:             .any(|candidate| candidate.disposition == disposition)
319:     };
320:     let disposition = if candidates.is_empty()
321:         || missing_evidence
322:         || empty_boundary
323:         || has(GovernanceDisposition::Deny)
324:     {
325:         GovernanceDisposition::Deny
326:     } else if has(GovernanceDisposition::Escalate) {
327:         GovernanceDisposition::Escalate
328:     } else if has(GovernanceDisposition::Boundary) {
329:         GovernanceDisposition::Boundary
330:     } else if has(GovernanceDisposition::Degraded) {
331:         if policy.allow_degraded && !compensating_controls.is_empty() {
332:             GovernanceDisposition::Degraded
333:         } else {
334:             GovernanceDisposition::Deny
335:         }
336:     } else {
337:         GovernanceDisposition::Allow
338:     };
339:     ResolvedGovernance {
340:         disposition,
341:         boundaries,
342:         compensating_controls,
343:     }
344: }

685: impl SelfDisclosureSurface {
686:     /// Validate the surface (§8.2): mode must be deny-by-default, claim
687:     /// classes must be known, high-risk grants need friction.
688:     pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), ForgeError> {
689:         if self.mode != "deny-by-default" {
690:             return Err(schema(
691:                 "self_disclosure.mode must be deny-by-default".into(),
692:             ));
693:         }
694:         for grant in &self.grants {
695:             for class in &grant.claim_classes {
696:                 if !VALID_CLAIM_CLASSES.contains(&class.as_str()) {
697:                     return Err(schema(format!(
698:                         "unknown claim class '{class}' in self_disclosure grant '{}'",
699:                         grant.name
700:                     )));
701:                 }
702:                 if HIGH_RISK_CLASSES.contains(&class.as_str())
703:                     && (!grant.explicit_high_risk
704:                         || grant
705:                             .compensating_control
706:                             .as_deref()
707:                             .unwrap_or("")
708:                             .is_empty())
709:                 {
710:                     return Err(schema(format!(
711:                         "high-risk class '{class}' in grant '{}' requires explicit_high_risk: true and a compensating control",
712:                         grant.name
713:                     )));
714:                 }
715:             }
716:         }
717:         Ok(())
718:     }
719: 
720:     /// Returns true if `actor_role` is permitted to disclose `claim_class`.
721:     /// Absent surface ⇒ deny (§8.2).

853:     pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, ForgeError> {
854:         let text = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| ForgeError::Config {
855:             class: "missing_config_error",
856:             path: path.into(),
857:             message: e.to_string(),
858:         })?;
859:         let yaml: serde_yaml::Value =
860:             serde_yaml::from_str(&text).map_err(|error| ForgeError::Config {
861:                 class: "parse_error",
862:                 path: path.into(),
863:                 message: error.location().map_or_else(
864:                     || "invalid YAML".into(),
865:                     |location| {
866:                         format!(
867:                             "invalid YAML at line {}, column {}",
868:                             location.line(),
869:                             location.column()
870:                         )
871:                     },
872:                 ),
873:             })?;
874:         let mut bundle: Self = serde_yaml::from_value(yaml).map_err(|_| ForgeError::Config {
875:             class: "schema_error",
876:             path: path.into(),
877:             message: "policy does not match the required schema".into(),
878:         })?;
879:         bundle.validate(path)?;
880:         if bundle.version == "0.2" {
881:             let base = bundle
882:                 .source_base
883:                 .clone()
884:                 .unwrap_or_else(|| path.parent().unwrap_or_else(|| Path::new(".")).into());
885:             for source in &bundle.sources {
886:                 let source_path = base.join(&source.path);
887:                 let bytes = fs::read(&source_path)
888:                     .map_err(|error| ForgeError::io("read authority policy source", error))?;
889:                 if source.sha256 != sha256_bytes(&bytes) {
890:                     return Err(ForgeError::Config {
891:                         class: "source_hash_mismatch",
892:                         path: source_path,
893:                         message: format!("authority source {} hash mismatch", source.surface),
894:                     });
895:                 }
896:             }
897:             bundle.source_base = Some(base);
898:         }
899:         Ok(bundle)
900:     }

964:             const SURFACES: &[&str] = &[

967:                 "domain_model",

981:                 "secret_access",
982:                 "policy_mutation",
983:                 "evidence_mutation",

985:             const ROLES: &[&str] = &["R-DS", "R-AG", "R-LC", "R-SO", "R-RM", "R-DEV", "R-AA"];
986:             // (name, operation_kind, optional transition_kind selector)
987:             const SOD: &[(&str, &str, Option<&str>)] = &[
988:                 ("production_proposer_approver", "pr_merge", None),

999:                     Some("capitalize"),

1002:             if self.bundle_id.as_deref().is_none_or(str::is_empty)
1003:                 || self.policy_bundle_hash.as_deref().is_none_or(str::is_empty)
1004:                 || self
1005:                     .policy_bundle_version
1006:                     .as_deref()
1007:                     .is_none_or(str::is_empty)
1008:                 || self.loaded_at.as_deref().is_none_or(str::is_empty)
1009:                 || SURFACES
1010:                     .iter()
1011:                     .any(|surface| !self.sources.iter().any(|source| source.surface == *surface))
1012:                 || ROLES.iter().any(|role| !self.roles.contains_key(*role))

1014:                     !self
1015:                         .permissions

1053:         self.policy_surfaces

1056:             .map_err(|e| ForgeError::Config {

1: # ADR-003: Public/persisted contract deltas for the four-spec audit remediation plan
2: 
3: ## Status
4: 
5: Accepted
6: 
7: ## Date
8: 
9: 2026-07-22
10: 
11: ## Context
12: 
13: `.agents/plans/2026-07-22-spec-audit-remediation.md` Task 0 requires an
14: inventory of additive policy/config/public-type changes needed by Tasks 1-18,
15: and owner approval of the compatibility approach before any task lands code.
16: The plan's guardrails forbid altering persisted schemas, policy precedence, ID
17: grammar, exit codes, or public interfaces without explicit approval — this ADR
18: is that approval, scoped to *additive* deltas only.
19: 
20: Before drafting the inventory, the repository was checked field-by-field
21: rather than assumed, because several items the plan's per-task steps describe
22: as needing new fields already exist from prior milestone work (M9-M16 landed
23: between this plan's audit and today per `git log`):
24: 
25: - `Operation::AgentTask` (`crates/sea-forge-core/src/types.rs:161-171`)
26:   **already carries** `response_schema: Option<serde_json::Value>` and
27:   `transcript_retention: Option<String>`. Tasks 15/16's defect is that
28:   `case_dispatch.rs` currently *drops* these fields on the floor, not that the
29:   fields are missing. **No new persisted field is needed for these two.**
30: - `PolicyRule.memory_scope: Option<String>` (`crates/sea-forge-authority/src/lib.rs:738`)
31:   **already exists**. Task 6's defect is that generic reserved-authority
32:   matching ignores it, not that it is absent. **No new field needed.**
33: - `OriginRefKind::DesiredOutcome`, `ItemKind::AgentTask`,
34:   `ManagerIteration` (with `case_id`/`iteration`/`snapshot_*`/`judgment`
35:   fields) and the M9 `ProjectionKind` self-model variants are **already
36:   landed and versioned** (see the in-code compatibility comments at
37:   `types.rs:659-663` and `:1199-1202`). These are cross-referenced, not
38:   re-approved, by this ADR.
39: 
40: This matters because it shrinks the genuinely new surface this ADR must
41: approve, and it establishes the compatibility convention already in
42: production use, which the remaining genuinely-new deltas below follow rather
43: than invent.
44: 
45: ## Established compatibility convention (already in production, not new)
46: 
47: Confirmed from four live precedents in `sea-forge-core::types`:
48: 
49: 1. **New optional struct field**: `#[serde(default)]` +
50:    `Option<T>` (+ `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` when the type
51:    should omit the field entirely on old-shape output). Old readers that
52:    don't know the field simply never populate it; new readers treat absence
53:    as "not set." Precedent: `PolicyRule.memory_scope`,
54:    `Operation::AgentTask.{response_schema,transcript_retention}`.
55: 2. **New enum variant, old readers structurally never see it**: append the
56:    variant; document (in a doc-comment on the variant) which record_kind or
57:    context gates its appearance so an old binary never deserializes a record
58:    that could contain it. Precedent: `ProjectionKind`'s M9 self-model
59:    variants (gated on `record_kind == self_model_projection` /
60:    `.sea-forge/self-model/`).
61: 3. **New enum variant, old readers may see it and must fail clean**: append
62:    the variant and accept that an old reader's `serde` deserialization
63:    returns `Err` (not a panic, not silent data loss) because the variant only
64:    appears in records a new-only code path produces. Precedent:
65:    `OriginRefKind::DesiredOutcome`.
66: 4. **No version bump for additive changes**: `RECORD_VERSION`/schema-tag
67:    values only change for a genuinely breaking shape change; purely additive
68:    deltas reuse the existing version and rely on (1)-(3) instead.
69: 
70: Every genuinely new delta below is approved under one of these three shapes,
71: not a fourth pattern.
72: 
73: ## Decision — genuinely new deltas by task
74: 
75: - **Task 5 (DomainForge source-set boundary, M0)**: new finite-limits +
76:   pinned-version fields on the adapter's source-set contract in
77:   `crates/sea-forge-domainforge/src/lib.rs` (not `sea-forge-core`, per
78:   ADR-001's boundary) — shape (1), additive `Option`/defaulted fields on a
79:   contract that is itself new-ish and not yet widely persisted across old
80:   records. `source_refs`/model identity gain these as required inputs to
81:   hashing, per the spec's stable-identity requirement.
82: - **Task 6 (memory authority scope, M4b)**: no new field (see Context above).
83:   Behavior-only: `crates/sea-forge-authority/src/lib.rs` must match
84:   `PolicyRule.memory_scope` against the exact requested target
85:   entity/process instead of ignoring it, and the canonical `recall_memory`
86:   action must include target scope so the decision hash changes when scope
87:   changes. This is an enforcement fix, not a contract delta, and needed no
88:   owner sign-off under the "no persisted schema change" guardrail — recorded
89:   here only so Task 6 is not blocked waiting for an ADR entry that isn't
90:   required.
91: - **Task 9 (spec-pipeline prerequisites, M5 library)**: shape (1) additive
92:   fields on the stage/input contract in `crates/sea-forge-spec-pipeline/src/lib.rs`
93:   naming immutable predecessor records (status, hash, schema, DomainModelRef,
94:   pinned DomainForge version) plus validation evidence refs. Only added if
95:   the existing `PlanItem`/stage vocabulary cannot already carry a predecessor
96:   reference — Task 9 step 2 keeps a small order helper if the addition can be
97:   avoided; this ADR pre-approves the addition in case it cannot.
98: - **Task 10A (M5 stage CasePlan, M5 runner)**: shape (1)/(2) — the smallest
99:   typed stage operation/metadata addition to `sea-forge-core::types`, added
100:   *only if* existing `Operation`/`ItemKind` vocabulary cannot carry Task 9's
101:   predecessor refs (Task 10A step 2 explicitly prefers reuse first).
102: - **Task 11 (self-model realization, M9)**: no new record types — the M9
103:   `ProjectionKind` self-model variants and snapshot/projection shapes already
104:   exist (see Context). The delta is behavior-only: populate the
105:   already-defined governance refs (authority/evidence/settlement) instead of
106:   leaving them empty, per the "Key facts" table.
107: - **Task 12 (ODI provenance, M10)**: no new persisted type — replaces
108:   `sha256:placeholder`/`outcome:primary` literal values in
109:   `crates/sea-forge-planner/src/templates.rs` with real resolved values in
110:   the *existing* `OriginRefKind::DesiredOutcome`-shaped fields. Behavior-only.
111: - **Task 13/13B (Thoth claims, M11)**: shape (1) — `authored_by` on

53:   deterministic build across dev machines and CI regardless of host OS

### 7.0a DomainForge semantic boundary (M0 contract; M2/M5 use)

`sea-forge-domainforge` is a first-party adapter around the canonical
`domainforge-core` Rust library. It is not part of `sea-forge-core`, and the
minimum kernel does not depend on it. Its public contract is synchronous and
side-effect-free:

```text
load_validate(SeaSourceSet) -> DomainModel
evaluate(DomainModel, CanonicalActionRequest, TrustedFacts) -> GovernanceVerdict
project(DomainModel, ProjectionRequest) -> SortedMap<RelativePath, Bytes>
```

**SeaSourceSet** contains one entry `.sea` source and any namespace-registry or
imported `.sea` files, each with workspace-relative URI and SHA-256. The adapter
MUST use DomainForge's namespace-aware parser. Absolute paths, unresolved
imports, source-hash changes, syntax errors, semantic validation errors, and
unsupported DomainForge versions fail before plan execution. The adapter
descriptor MUST declare finite limits for source count, aggregate bytes, import
depth, AST nodes, and parser work; exceeding any limit is `domain_model_error`,
not a reason to retry with weaker validation.

**DomainModel** is an in-memory derived view, not a second persisted truth. Each
governed consumer records a **DomainModelRef** containing:

- `source_refs`: sorted non-empty array of `{uri, sha256}` covering the entry
  source, namespace registry, and resolved imports.
- `domainforge_version`, `adapter_descriptor_sha256`, and
  `parse_options_sha256` (canonical hash of namespace/profile/parser options).
- `semantic_model_sha256`: SHA-256 of canonical
  `{domainforge_version, adapter_descriptor_sha256, parse_options_sha256,
  source_refs}`. This identifies the exact validated semantic input without
  depending on an unstable serialization of DomainForge's in-memory Graph.
- `concept_refs`: sorted array of canonical DomainForge concept IDs actually
  consulted by the plan, authority evaluation, or projection.
- `validation_evidence_refs`: non-empty refs proving parse and semantic
  validation results.

The plan, DomainForge candidate verdict, projection record, and semantic
envelope MUST reference the same `DomainModelRef` when they concern the same
world model. A source or version change creates a new ref; no run silently
rebinds to a different world.

`CasePlan`, `CanonicalActionRequest`, and `SemanticEnvelope` each gain optional
`domain_model_ref` and sorted `concept_refs` fields in v0.2. The fields are
REQUIRED when the plan or action is scoped to a `.sea` world and absent for
unbound legacy work. DomainForge `GovernanceVerdict` evidence resolves the same
ref rather than embedding a second copy of the model.

DomainForge authority normalization is fixed:

| DomainForge result | SEA Forge candidate disposition |
|---|---|
| `Reject` or `Deny` | `deny` |
| `Escalate` | `escalate` |
| `Allow` | `allow` |
| `NotApplicable` | no candidate; `deny` if policy requires DomainForge for the surface |

The adapter MUST preserve the DomainForge trace as evidence and include the
consulted `DomainModelRef`. SEA Forge then combines this candidate with hard
boundaries and all other configured engines using §7.0 precedence. DomainForge
never emits the final SEA Forge `AuthorityDecision`.

Projection MUST use DomainForge's in-memory artifact sink or equivalent public
library API. The adapter returns bytes and relative paths; only SEA Forge may
authorize and materialize them. The built-in path MUST NOT let DomainForge write
the workspace, invoke external tools, or access the network directly.

### 7.0b Extension and projection ABI (M0 contract, M5+ use)

The minimum spec defines `ExtensionDescriptor` and `ProjectionRef`. Full spec persists and enforces them.

**ExtensionRegistry** (`.sea-forge/extensions/registry.json`):

- `version`, `updated_at`.
- `extensions`: array of `{extension_id, version, descriptor_sha256, trust_level, status}`.
- `trust_level` (enum: `built_in | first_party | workspace | imported | quarantined`).
- `status` (enum: `active | disabled | quarantined | superseded`).

## Summary

### Task 6 — Bind memory scope into authority grants ✅

**Outcome:** `recall_memory` authorization now binds the requested target entity/process via `memory_scope`, and the returned `ActionGrant` carries the scope boundary.

**Changed files:**
- `crates/sea-forge-authority/src/lib.rs` — added `scope_allows` pub fn, `matches_memory_scope` helper, `recall_memory` branch in `matches_rule`, `memory_scope: Option<String>` field on `ActionGrant` + `memory_scope()` accessor, set in `grant_exact`; modified legacy v0.1 read path to not preempt when a `recall_memory` rule exists.
- `crates/sea-forge-authority/tests/conformance_m0_authority.rs` — 8 new tests: own (allow/deny), entity (allow/deny), any, missing scope (deny), hash-changes-with-target, grant-carries-boundary.
- `crates/sea-forge-capability/src/memory.rs` — removed orphaned `scope_allows` (moved to authority).
- `crates/sea-forge-capability/tests/conformance_m4b.rs` — removed `scope_allows` import + test.
- `crates/sea-forge-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs` — added `"memory_scope": "any"` to the `allow-recall` fixture rule (required by the new enforcement).

**Gate:** `cargo test -p sea-forge-authority --test conformance_m0_authority memory_scope` → 8 passed.

### Task 5 — DomainForge source-set trust boundary ✅

**Outcome:** `load_validate` verifies every source URI/hash, resolves imports from the supplied set, enforces finite limits, and rejects unsupported versions before returning a `DomainModelRef`.

**Changed files:**
- `crates/sea-forge-domainforge/src/lib.rs` — rewrote `load_validate` with: version guard, all-file hash verification, URI validation (absolute/traversal/duplicate), finite limits (source count, aggregate bytes, AST nodes, import depth), in-memory import resolution (namespace map, export checking, cycle detection), `source_refs` from all verified files, parse_options hash includes version+limits.
- `crates/sea-forge-domainforge/tests/conformance_m0_domainforge.rs` — 11 new tests: multi-file resolved import, unresolved import, non-entry hash drift, duplicate URI, absolute/traversal URI, source count limit, aggregate bytes limit, version guard, no-source-error-reaches-planning, source_refs include all files.

**Gate:** `cargo test -p sea-forge-domainforge --test conformance_m0_domainforge` → 16 passed. `cargo test -p sea-forge-domainforge --test projection` → 5 passed.

### Task 5 redesign trigger — import resolution

**Finding:** The pinned `domainforge-core =0.13.0`'s `ModuleResolver` reads import dependencies from the filesystem (`fs::read_to_string`). It cannot accept an in-memory `SeaSourceSet`. This is exactly the trigger condition.

**What I did (the "smallest supported adapter change"):** Implemented adapter-side in-memory import resolution using the pinned library's **public parse API** (`parse_source`, `ast_to_graph_with_options`). This:
- Parses every file in-memory — no filesystem, no CLI, no temp files.
- Builds namespace→file map, validates imports resolve within the set, checks named exports, detects cycles, enforces import depth.
- Builds the graph from the entry AST — **identical behavior** to the pinned library's own resolver path (which also builds from the entry AST only; module resolution is validation-only).

**Deviation surfaced:** Step 3 says "Use the pinned DomainForge namespace-aware library API." I use the library's public parser/graph-builder APIs but not its `ModuleResolver` (which is filesystem-only). The namespace awareness is implemented in the adapter over the library's public AST types. Zero new dependencies, no fs staging, no CLI.

If you want a different approach (e.g., bump domainforge-core, or restrict the adapter to single-file models until the library supports in-memory resolution), say so and I'll revise.

**Proof:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean. All 26 affected test suites pass (authority 40+17, cli 44+11, capability 13+7, domainforge 16+5, plus downstream: self-model, spec-pipeline, artifact-ip — 0 failures).
